fr:mainmatter.fr:p:
Each C-c C-l, C-c C-, takes so long, it's difficult to do focused work. I delineate "fast enough" from "too slow" when I find myself either
Finding other low-attention work to do on the computer-- like filling out forms-- while I'm waiting for emacs to color the agda buffer and stop saying 'Agda is busy with something'
Doing literally anything else on the computer, which usually ends up being r*dd*t, much to the detriment of my productivity

fr:ul.fr:li: Enable {-# OPTIONS --lossy-unification #-} at the top of the current agda file
Comment out (especially slow) parts of the current agda file that you don't strictly need to work on this hole This is usually the easiest, most effective hammer.

Use opaque. Something simple but I only just realized after a lot of head banging: If you use _ in a type, opaque can't export the type. You have to C-c C-s the hole first, and export the potentially very ugly proof term. This is typically used to make expensive path proofs opaque. The types of the path need to be non-opaque to be useful.

Build Agda with the cabal flag cabal configure -f optimise-heavily, and maybe try the cabal.project(.local) option optimization: 2? Newer versions of Agda may not be able to infer all of the same _ holes, so maybe checkout v2.7.0.1 or what have you. This kind of works? TODO: Benchmark?

I haven't been able to get any positive result by tinkering with the ghc runtime settings +RTS -RTS. About \frac {1}{4} of the time is spent in GC. I tried to offload some of that work to another cpu, but was not successful in my attempts.
